Early tester of Mistral OCR: 'Super fast and significantly more accurate than google, Claude and others.' Found it great at PDF to markdown, but was confused about what 'batched' pricing ($1/1000 pages, or 2k pages batched) actually means.

Layperson tried OCR'ing hundreds of pages through the Le Chat interface, but it stopped after the 2nd page. Submitting via the API instead worked, though they had to split the document into smaller chunks because 900 pages at once ended in a timeout.

Tester (who runs a competing tool) found Mistral OCR super fast and synchronous, but on their document it treated the entire page as an image. It returned `![img-0.jpeg](img-0.jpeg)` with coordinates for a single image covering the whole page instead of extracting the text.

Tested a multilingual bidi English/Hebrew document: the Hebrew output had no correspondence to the actual text. It was a back-translation of the English translation in the document. Benchmarks are impressive but disappointing for humanities multilingual scans; also noted it doesn't return bounding boxes for text.
Commenter says Mistral OCR outperforms the competition significantly and can extract embedded images from the text, adding they increasingly prefer LLMs for OCR (Gemini was already pretty good).

Used the predecessor Mistral OCR model to process 55-year-old paper files, most severely degraded, and was very impressed. Also tried Abbyy FineReader, which 'didn't even come close' in their experience.

'We have successfully used Mistral OCR for digitizing handwritten forms. You always have low percentage that need human review and adjustment, but overall Mistral has been highly accurate (their price is amazing, too).'
